title: Flat groupoid quotient presentations and invariant open restriction
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and stacks, representability and 2-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable morphism properties are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Flatness, local finite presentation, etaleness and properness use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A stack morphism is separated if its relative diagonal is proper. The inertia stack $I_{\mathcal A}$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows given by conjugating isomorphisms. Its projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The set $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the atlas topology [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. A scheme groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ has the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Its quotient $[U/R]$ is the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $T$-points, using [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Finite locally free means finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid of $k$-schemes with $s,t$ flat and locally of finite presentation. Then $\mathcal Q=[U/R]$ is an algebraic stack and $p:U\to\mathcal Q$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, with canonical equivalence $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$. If $s,t$ are finite, then $p$ is finite (every scheme base change is a finite scheme morphism), and $p$ is of finite presentation. Pullback gives an inclusion-preserving bijection between open substacks $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal Q$ and open subschemes $V\subseteq U$ satisfying $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$. Under this bijection $U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W=V$ and $\mathcal W\simeq[V/R_V]$, where $R_V=s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$. The restricted projections are the base changes of $s,t$, so are finite locally free when $s,t$ are. Every point of $|\mathcal Q|$ lifts to a point of $U$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the given scheme groupoid, regarded as a groupoid in algebraic spaces. Its hypotheses are exactly flatness and local finite presentation of $s,t$. It gives algebraicity of $\mathcal Q$, representability, surjectivity, flatness and local finite presentation of $p$, and $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ with projections $s,t$. Its field-extension lifting clause also gives immediately the asserted surjectivity $|U|\to|\mathcal Q|$.

Suppose $s,t$ are finite. For a scheme $T\to\mathcal Q$, let $F=U\times_{\mathcal Q}T$, an algebraic space by step 1. The local-description theorem [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] supplies an fppf cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ and lifts $u_i:T_i\to U$ of the object on $T$. The tuple definition of the 2-fibre product and step 1 identify $F\times_TT_i$ with $R\times_{s,U,u_i}T_i$, respecting its map to $T_i$. This scheme map is a base change of the finite morphism $s$, hence finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], and by the same node so is each of its scheme base changes. The family $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]: jointly surjective, with flat locally finitely presented members. Hence [lem-sfb-space-finite-fppf-descent], applied to $F\to T$ and this covering, makes $F\to T$ finite on every scheme test; taking the test $T$ itself, $F$ is a scheme finite over $T$. This proves finiteness of $p$ on every scheme test. By the definition of a finite scheme morphism it is affine, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with the local finite presentation from step 1, this gives finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated).

proof.text: Pullback of any open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal Q$ is an open subscheme $V\subseteq U$. The two pullbacks to $R=U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$ coincide: a point of the 2-fibre product comes with an isomorphism between its images in $\mathcal Q$, and membership in a strictly full substack is invariant under that isomorphism. Pullback preserves inclusion. These assertions use only the definitions of open substack and 2-fibre product in [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] and [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

Conversely fix an invariant open $V\subseteq U$. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:A\to\mathcal Q$, available by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and put $E=U\times_{\mathcal Q}A$, with $h:E\to U$ and $q:E\to A$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $h$ is smooth surjective and $q$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective. In particular they are surjective on point sets by [lem-sfb-representable-stack-point-surjectivity]. Put $D=h^{-1}(V)$ and $B=q(|D|)\subseteq A$. This is open by [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open], so give it its open subscheme structure. We claim $q^{-1}(B)=D$. If $e$ lies over a point of $B$, choose $d\in|D|$ over that same point. The point-surjectivity of fibre products in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives a common-field representative of $(e,d)$ in $E\times_AE$. Their $U$-coordinates and the two comparison isomorphisms give an arrow of $U\times_{\mathcal Q}U=R$. One endpoint lies in $V$, so invariance puts the other in $V$. This proves saturation. Equality of open point subsets is equality of open subspaces by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image].

source.place: Tag 0507, invariant-open construction via a smooth atlas; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S

proof.text: The open $B$ is invariant under $A\times_{\mathcal Q}A$. Indeed, represent an arrow by $\alpha:a(a_1)\simeq a(a_2)$ over a field. After field extension, lift $a_1$ to $e=(u,a_1,\beta)$ in $E$, using surjectivity of $q$. Saturation from step 4 says $a_1\in B$ exactly when $u\in V$. Composing $\beta$ with $\alpha$ produces $(u,a_2,\alpha\beta)\in E$, so $u\in V$ implies $a_2\in B$. Apply the inverse arrow for the reverse implication. Open subspaces are determined by point subsets by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], hence the two inverse-image opens on $A\times_{\mathcal Q}A$ agree. Now [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], applied to the smooth atlas $A$, gives an open substack $\mathcal W$ with $A\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W=B$.

source.place: Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), applied to the smooth atlas A

proof.text: Its pullback $V'=U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W$ is an open subscheme. On $E$ its pullback is $q^{-1}(B)=h^{-1}(V)$ by step 4. Since $h$ is surjective, $V'=V$. If $\mathcal W'$ is any other open substack with pullback $V$, its pullback $B'$ to $A$ satisfies $q^{-1}(B')=h^{-1}(V)=q^{-1}(B)$; surjectivity of $q$ gives $B'=B$, and uniqueness in [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] gives $\mathcal W'=\mathcal W$. Finally $V_1\subseteq V_2$ implies $D_1\subseteq D_2$, hence $B_1\subseteq B_2$; inclusion preservation in the same node gives $\mathcal W_1\subseteq\mathcal W_2$. These calculations prove both directions of the inclusion-preserving bijection.

source.place: Tag 0507, uniqueness and inclusion preservation; common-atlas argument

proof.text: The open substack $\mathcal W$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]: it is a strictly full substack of the etale stack $\mathcal Q$ whose membership is tested by open subschemes, hence etale-local, so it is an etale stack; since $\mathcal W\to\mathcal Q$ is fully faithful, $T\times_{\mathcal W\times\mathcal W}\mathcal W=T\times_{\mathcal Q\times\mathcal Q}\mathcal Q$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal W\times\mathcal W$, so its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces; and $B=A\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W\to\mathcal W$ is a base change of the smooth surjective atlas $a$, hence a smooth surjective scheme atlas by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. By base change from step 1, $V=U\times_{\mathcal Q}\mathcal W\to\mathcal W$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, using [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Its self 2-fibre product is the restriction of $R$ to both endpoints in $V$. Invariance identifies this with $R_V=s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)$: an arrow has both endpoints in $V$ exactly when either endpoint is in $V$. The groupoid operations restrict because identities, inverse and composition retain endpoints. Clause (2) of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations], applied to $V\to\mathcal W$, now gives $\mathcal W\simeq[V/R_V]$ compatibly with the map from $V$.

The restricted source and target maps are literally $R\times_{s,U}V\to V$ and $R\times_{t,U}V\to V$: equality of the two inverse-image opens identifies their sources with $R_V$. Flatness and local finite presentation survive these base changes by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], and finiteness survives by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Hence if $s,t$ are finite locally free, so are the restricted projections, by the definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free].
